sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 116 of 2012
Judgement:
The appellant is 4th respondent/Insurance company and respondents are claim petitioners and
respondent Nos.1 to 3 in M.V.O.P.No.368 of 2009 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal-cum-Judge, Family Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Guntur.

The appellant
filed the appeal questioning the legal validity of the order of the Tribunal.
2.  For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claim petitioners filed a claim petition under Section 163- A and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards compensation for the death of Ponnuru Anjaneyulu in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.11.2006.
VGKR,J 4.

The brief averments of the claim petition are as follows:
On 28.11.2006 the deceased was returning from Penuganchiprolu on a motor cycle bearing registration No.AP 07AJ 6250, which was being driven by the 3rd respondent, as a pillion rider and when they reached Tobacco Board near Kesara village of N.H.9, a lorry bearing registration No.AP 24W 0070 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed, came in opposite direction and dashed the motor cycle.
As a result of which, the deceased sustained severe head injuries and succumbed to injuries on the way to hospital.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are owner and insurer of the lorry and respondent Nos.3 and 4 are owner and insurer of the motor cycle, respectively.
Therefore, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
5. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 were set ex parte.
6. The 4th respondent/Insurance company filed a written statement by denying the manner of accident.

It is pleaded that the VGKR,J rider of the motor cycle had no valid and affective driving licence at the time of accident and the police registered a case against the driver of the lorry involved in the accident and hence, the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.
Bajaj Allianz
General

sentences.text:
1 7. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues for trial:
1. Whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the drivers of (i) Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP 24W 0070 (ii) Yamaha Motor Bike No.AP 07AJ 6250?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to the compensation, if so, from whom? and 3.
To what relief?
8. During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners, P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A.1 to A.3 were marked.
On behalf of the 4th respondent, R.W.1 was examined and Exs.B.1 and B.2 were marked.
VGKR,J 9.

At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.2,10,000/- towards compensation to the claim petitioners.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the 4th respondent/Insurance company filed the appeal.

10. Heard learned counsels for both the parties.
11.

The grounds urged by the appellant/Insurance company are that the Tribunal failed to see that Ex.A.1-first information report was registered and Ex.A.2-charge sheet was filed against the driver of the lorry and also Ex.B.2-rough sketch which shows that the offending lorry came on wrong side and dashed the motor cycle.
12.

Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order passed by the Tribunal needs any interference?
13. POINT:

The learned Tribunal framed an issue i.e., "whether the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the drivers of (i) Lorry bearing Regn.No.AP 24W 0070 (ii) Yamaha VGKR,J Motor Bike No.AP 07AJ 6250?", and found that the 4th respondent/Insurance company also cannot escape from its liability in respect of the deceased who was, admittedly, travelling on the motor cycle in question as a pillion rider.
The 4th respondent is the insurer of the motor cycle and filed the appeal against the award passed by the Tribunal.

As seen from the material on record, on 28.11.2006 the deceased was returning from Penuganchiprolu on a motor cycle bearing registration No.AP 07AJ 6250, which was being driven by the 3rd respondent, as a pillion rider and when they reached Tobacco Board near Kesara village of N.H.9, a lorry bearing registration No.AP 24W 0070 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed, came in opposite direction and dashed the motor cycle, due to which, the deceased sustained severe head injuries and succumbed to injuries on the way to hospital.

sentences.text: In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry, the petitioners relied on the evidence of P.W.2, who is the rider of the motor cycle at the time of accident.
As per his VGKR,J evidence, he was driving the motor cycle and the deceased was a pillion rider on his motor cycle.
On 18.06.2009 at about 4.30 p.m. when they were proceeding near Kesara village, the offending lorry came in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motor cycle.
The F.I.R. was registered against the driver of the offending lorry under Ex.A.1 and charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the offending lorry under Ex.A.2.
Ex.A.1- first information report was not at all registered against the rider of the motor cycle, who is P.W.2 in this case.
The police, after completion of investigation, laid charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry.

As per the rough sketch drawn by the police, the offending lorry came on wrong side and dashed against the motor cycle, on which the deceased was travelling, and the same was supported by Exs.A.1 and A.2.

But, the learned Tribunal failed to take into consideration all the above aspects and came to conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle and the driver of the offending lorry.
For the VGKR,J foregoing reasons, this Court finds that the accident occurred due to pure rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
15. As per the case of the claim petitioners, the 1st respondent is the owner of the offending lorry.
The 1st respondent insured the offending lorry with the 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the policy number and its validity were mentioned in the claim application.
Respondent Nos.1 to 3 were set ex parte, for the reasons best known to them.
The 2nd respondent did not deny that the offending lorry is not insured with the Insurance company.
16. The learned Tribunal, after giving cogent reasons, awarded compensation of Rs.2,10,000/- to the claim petitioners.
No appeal is filed by the claim petitioners against the said finding.
The learned Tribunal in its order held that the deceased was a Bachelor and he was unmarried and the age of the mother can be taken as basis for adopting suitable multiplier.
The age of the mother of the deceased was shown as 45 years and his father's age was shown as 55 years.

So, the multiplier applicable to the age group of the mother of the deceased was taken by the Tribunal as "11" and the income of the VGKR,J deceased was arrived at Rs.3,000/- p.m. and the annual income was arrived at Rs.36,000/-
which is not at all challenged by the claim petitioners.
The learned Tribunal failed to consider the age of the deceased by the date of accident.
But, the said finding is not at all challenged by the claim petitioners.

After deducting 50% of income towards personal expenses of the deceased, the net loss of dependency was arrived at Rs.18,000/- p.a. and the gross loss of dependency was arrived at Rs.1,98,000/- (Rs.18,000/- x 11).
The Tribunal also awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.2,000/- towards funeral expenses.

In total, the Tribunal awarded Rs.2,10,000/-
towards compensation.
The same is not challenged by the claim petitioners by filing an appeal for enhancement of compensation.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

17. The pleadings of the petition itself reveal that the offending lorry was insured by the 1st respondent with the 2nd respondent/Insurance company and the policy was also in force on the date of accident.
It is not the case of the 2nd VGKR,J respondent/Insurance company that there are violations in the said policy.

For the reasons best known to them, respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co Ltd vs Ponnuru Koteswara Rao 4 Ors on 8 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163071179/
3 turn up and they were set ex parte in the claim petition.

sentences.text: For the foregoing reasons, this Court holds that the accident occurred due to pure rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry and therefore, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly liable to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
18. In the result, the appeal is allowed.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are directed to pay the compensation of Rs.2,10,000/- with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization, as awarded by the Tribunal.
The claim application against respondent Nos.3 and 4 is dismissed.

The order and decree dated 06.04.2010 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Judge, Family Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Guntur, in M.V.O.P.No.368 of 2009 is modified to the extent indicated above.
